topic_candidates.title: OpenAI Says It Just Did the Impossible — But What Does That Mean?
topic_candidates.query: OpenAI October 2026 Exponential Time Hypothesis false Lean formalized proof explanation
topic_candidates.brief: OpenAI says its AI system produced a result refuting the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a major assumption about how difficult some computer problems are. The video explains the claim without pretending it solves P versus NP, breaks encryption or makes every hard problem easy. The key story is the verification pipeline: AI proposes a proof, researchers examine it, and Lean checks whether the formal steps follow logically.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: OpenAI says its system produced a natural-language disproof on October 16, 2026, formalized it in Lean on October 17, and released the output for outside experts to examine. The company also says any practical algorithmic benefit will require further research, so the video should frame this as a significant claim under scrutiny rather than a settled revolution. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/building-scientific-understanding-with-academic-communities/?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: Breakout 9 — Two Minute Papers: “OpenAI Claims It Just Did The Impossible” — 279,677 views, 23,156 views/hour, 1.8× channel breakout.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Computational complexity, formal verification, proof assistants and the difference between a theorem result and a useful real-world algorithm.

topic_candidates.query: Google Gemini 4 Carbon October 2026 cybersecurity long horizon AI model benchmarks access price
topic_candidates.brief: Google’s new model is aimed less at casual chat and more at long-running coding and cybersecurity work. The video translates the benchmark claims into a practical question: can an AI agent find, test and fix a software vulnerability reliably, or does it still need expert supervision? It also explains why access is initially limited to trusted cyber defenders and why stronger models create both defensive and offensive capabilities.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon leads its reported cybersecurity tests, including vulnerability discovery, exploitation validation and patching, but is initially being rolled out to a limited group of cyber defenders before wider access. Those are company-reported results, so the story should distinguish benchmark performance from independent real-world proof. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/?utm_source=openai))
